## How to read this

**Nothing here decides that a requirement is met.** The strongest claim it makes is that the code *appears* to cover a capability, because a file is named for it or the reading identified it as a component. Whether what exists actually satisfies the requirement is a judgement, and it is yours.

What this does is narrow the judgement. Instead of reading 38 capabilities against a codebase, you read the 24 below that are unclear or absent.

Coverage matters here: this was decided from 66 files read out of 366 in the repository. A capability marked *not found* in a thin reading may simply be somewhere that was not read.

## Where to start

The build plan that ships with this specification contains only the capabilities above that are not already built. It is written to be picked up on the existing codebase rather than on an empty directory — no project scaffolding, no first commit, no re-creation of what is already running.

If a capability below is marked *not found* and you know it exists, say so and re-read with a wider budget: the reading is bounded, and a bounded reading has blind spots rather than opinions.
